newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed firmer on Friday, bouncing back from Thursday's stiff losses as retail and institutional investors ignored higher than expected German M3 money supply data, encouraged by gains in Bunds and Treasuries.
Dealers said part of the gains, most pronounced at the longer end where the 7.50 percent 2023 bond gained 0.72 to 114.16/36, occurred after Bunds bounced off technical support on Thursday.
"There's strong technical support around 100.95 and people feel one money supply figure doesn't really give that much reason for the Bundesbank to hike rates," a dealer said.

German May M3 money supply data released Thursday morning showed a 7.0 percent annualised rise, up from 6.7 percent in April, against estimates for a 6.4 percent rise. "I expected the market to come off on German M3 and still do," said the dealer.

"The figure was a bit of a surprise but people are taking it calmly, people believe the Buba can get M3 back in the range and will look at a lot of other indicators before they hike rates," another dealer said.
Retail and institutional investors concentrated on the longer end picking out value in a segment which dropped by around a point on Thursday in reaction to U.S. economic data.
A Reuters survey of six economists and dealers found they expected five year, 10 year and long Dutch bond yields to rise slightly over the next month.

They also forecast a narrowing of the five year and 10 year yield differential below Germany. The average 10 year yield estimate in one month's time is 5.69 percent versus 5.59 late on Friday. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
